correctness.rationale: A first block of size greater than one gives multiple sources and therefore no out-branching. In each listed exception the orientation forces every edge incident to one distinguished vertex into every possible branching, so deleting the branching isolates that vertex. For every other singleton-first code, the four constructive cases in the package choose one earlier opposite-part parent for every non-source vertex and exhibit explicit paths in the unused-edge complement connecting all three vertices of the small part and all remaining vertices of the large part. Rechecking the boundary case \(n=4\) confirms that every auxiliary choice of distinct large-part vertices still exists. The frozen verifier exhausts all block words through \(n=7\) by parent enumeration and tests the constructive schemes through \(n=30\); those checks support the explicit all-n proof rather than replacing it.

value.rationale: The family is the first complete-bipartite case with enough edges to support two edge-disjoint spanning trees, and the theorem gives a complete orientation-by-orientation classification rather than an algorithmic decision black box. Four exact obstruction codes are a natural structural answer to the motivating non-separating branching problem.

final_claim: For every \(n\ge4\), an acyclic orientation of \(K_{3,n}\) has a non-separating out-branching exactly when its canonical alternating source-removal code starts with a singleton and is not one of the four displayed obstruction families \(A^1B^nA^2\), \(A^1B^1A^2B^{n-1}\), \(B^1A^3B^{n-1}\), or \(B^1A^1B^{n-1}A^2\).
